record_type_quote: An additional goal of this research was to examine whether Masip and Herrero’s (2015) findings (obtained with middle-aged, mostly [77%] male, community members and police officers) could be replicated with a different sample of participants (younger, mostly female, college students).

targets.title: Police detection of deception: Beliefs about behavioral cues to deception are strong even though contextual evidence is more useful.
targets.evidence_quote: An additional goal of this research was to examine whether Masip and Herrero’s (2015) findings (obtained with middle-aged, mostly [77%] male, community members and police officers) could be replicated with a different sample of participants (younger, mostly female, college students).
targets.outcome_quote: Regardless of the focus of Q2, and in line with prior research, behavioral cues were reported less often, and contextual indicators more often, in responding to Q2 than in responding to Q1. However, contrary to prior findings, behavioral cues still predominated in the responses to Q2.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The original comparison between questionnaires replicated, but the original predominance of contextual over behavioral cues in revealing information was explicitly contradicted. Other papers discussed as prior literature are not independently targeted.

reasoning: The stated replication uses new student participants to re-test Masip and Herrero (2015), with additional question-focus conditions.
